All 24 tests pass. The implementation in `list_ops.py` covers all eight operations from the spec, each written without relying on existing list functions:

- **`append`** — builds a new list by iterating over both inputs
- **`concat`** — flattens one level by iterating each sublist
- **`filter`** — keeps items where the predicate is truthy
- **`length`** — counts via iteration (no `len`)
- **`map`** — applies the function to each item
- **`foldl`** — left-to-right iteration, calling `function(acc, item)`
- **`foldr`** — recursive: applies `function(acc, last_item)` then folds the rest, preserving the right-to-left order (this makes the direction-dependent tests like `el / acc` pass: `foldr` on `[1,2,3,4]` with `24` yields `9`)
- **`reverse`** — prepends each item to build the reversed list (no `reversed`/slicing)
